Today’s M&A briefing — one deal, the strategy behind it · 28 October 2026

🔹 Blue Soft (digital services, business applications, cybersecurity, data, infrastructure, work environments, change management for businesses) finalizes the acquisition of Roxys (microsoft services, identity, security, collaborative work, workstation management, change management for organizations, Arras).
Blue Soft (950 employees, €106M revenue in 2025, nine cities in France and Switzerland) acquires Roxys (€3.28M revenue in 2025, founded in 2012), previously absent from its network.
Our view: For a mid-sized digital services group, the real barrier to entry is not technical: it's capillarity. Blue Soft is building this barrier deal after deal, city after city.

en.text:
Today’s fundraising briefing — 2 deals, the strategies behind them · 28 October 2026

🔹 AQQI (personal AI assistant for real estate purchase journey management, administrative procedures, follow-ups, visits, coordination) — more than €55m.
AQQI was founded in early 2026 by two Studapart alumni (platform sold for over €55M). According to the company, the solution reduces by 75% the time-consuming tasks of a purchase journey that averages 150 hours and over a hundred exchanges.
Use of funds: Deployment to 1,000 buyers before public launch in early 2027, after tests in Île-de-France, Bordeaux, and Marseille.
Investors: Axeleo and Aquiti (co-leads); Kima Ventures, Pierre Kosciusko-Morizet, 50 Partners.
Our view: The challenge in the coming months will be to demonstrate a sufficiently high conversion rate and value to justify the acquisition cost in a market where buyers do not behave like subscribers.

🔹 Atlas Bio (AI platform for in silico clinical trial simulation to predict candidate drug behavior in Phase II) — $10m · Seed.
Atlas Bio simultaneously announces a $2.5M pre-seed and a $10M seed, totaling $12.5M.
Investors: Creandum (lead, partner Katharina Wilhelm on the board); previous pre-seed led by First Momentum Ventures and LEA Partners.
Our view: For an industrial partner or a corporate pharmaceutical investor, Atlas Bio represents an asymmetric bet: if validation holds, the value created is immeasurable compared to the $12.5 million committed.

fr.text:
Levées de fonds : les 2 opérations chiffrées de l'édito du 28 octobre 2026.

🔹 AQQI (𝑎𝑠𝑠𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑛𝑡 𝐼𝐴 𝑝𝑒𝑟𝑠𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑙 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑙𝑎 𝑔𝑒𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑢 𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑐𝑜𝑢𝑟𝑠 𝑑'𝑎𝑐ℎ𝑎𝑡 𝑖𝑚𝑚𝑜𝑏𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑒𝑟, 𝑑𝑒́𝑚𝑎𝑟𝑐ℎ𝑒𝑠 𝑎𝑑𝑚𝑖𝑛𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑣𝑒𝑠, 𝑟𝑒𝑙𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒𝑠, 𝑣𝑖𝑠𝑖𝑡𝑒𝑠) — plus de 55 M€.
AQQI est fondée début 2026 par deux anciens de Studapart (plateforme cédée pour plus de 55 M€). La solution réduit selon la société de 75 % les tâches chronophages d'un parcours d'achat qui mobilise en moyenne 150 heures et plus d'une centaine d'échanges.
Objectif : Déploiement à 1 000 acquéreurs avant lancement grand public début 2027, après tests en Île-de-France, Bordeaux et Marseille.
Avec : Axeleo et Aquiti (co-chefs de file) ; Kima Ventures, Pierre Kosciusko-Morizet, 50 Partners.
Point de vue : L'enjeu des prochains mois sera de démontrer un taux de conversion et une valeur suffisamment élevés pour justifier le coût d'acquisition dans un marché où les acheteurs ne se comportent pas comme des abonnés.

🔹 Atlas Bio (𝑝𝑙𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑒 𝐼𝐴 𝑑𝑒 𝑠𝑖𝑚𝑢𝑙𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑'𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑎𝑖𝑠 𝑐𝑙𝑖𝑛𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒𝑠 𝑖𝑛 𝑠𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑐𝑜 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑝𝑟𝑒́𝑑𝑖𝑟𝑒 𝑙𝑒 𝑐𝑜𝑚𝑝𝑜𝑟𝑡𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑑𝑒 𝑚𝑒́𝑑𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑠 𝑐𝑎𝑛𝑑𝑖𝑑𝑎𝑡𝑠 𝑒𝑛 𝑃ℎ𝑎𝑠𝑒 𝐼𝐼) — 10 M$ · Seed.
Atlas Bio annonce simultanément un pré-seed de 2,5 M$ et un seed de 10 M$, soit 12,5 M$ au total.
Avec : Creandum (chef de file, partenaire Katharina Wilhelm au CA) ; pré-seed précédent mené par First Momentum Ventures et LEA Partners.
Point de vue : Pour un partenaire industriel ou un investisseur corporate pharmaceutique, Atlas Bio représente un pari asymétrique : si la validation tient, la valeur créée est sans commune mesure avec les 12,5 millions engagés.
